OPEN SCIENCE, HONEST ASSUMPTIONS

Follow every drop.

A small, transparent model for exploring a big urban question.

01 / HYDROLOGY

A storm becomes a water budget.

Rainfall is applied to every 8 × 8 m cell. Roof runoff is directed to its nearest ground cell. Land-cover infiltration and finite intervention reservoirs remove water from the surface. Sewer inlets and the river are tracked outflows.

Rain = Surface + Stored + Infiltrated + Outflow
02 / FLOW

Terrain gives water a direction.

A finite-volume grid exchanges water across shared faces, driven by differences in water-surface elevation. A Manning-inspired discharge law uses depth, slope and surface roughness. Donor limiting preserves nonnegative depths and conserves exchanged water.

q ∝ h5/3 · √slope / roughness
03 / SEARCH

Test. Measure. Improve.

The optimizer ranks wet locations, diversifies candidate sites, and reruns the whole storm for each proposal. It accepts the greatest improvement per dollar, subject to your budget. The objective combines peak surface volume and flooded area. This is a greedy heuristic, not a guaranteed global optimum.

score = Δ(peak m³ + 0.035 × peak m²) / cost
04 / ACCESS

A route that sees the water.

A* searches the walkable grid at the selected simulation minute. Building and river cells are excluded. Cells above 15 cm are blocked; shallow water and unpaved ground add travel cost. The route illustrates network accessibility in this model.

f(n) = travel cost + Manhattan heuristic

Know the boundaries.

Riverside Commons is a synthetic 384 × 320 m neighborhood. Elevations, infiltration rates, storage capacities, inlet discharges and costs are illustrative. The model has a 10-second time step, closed outer boundaries, a free-draining river edge and no subsurface sewer network, infiltration recovery, backwater or erosion. It is an educational prototype, not a calibrated flood forecast or engineering design tool. Street routing is a teaching visualization, not real-world navigation.

Conceptual reference: US EPA Storm Water Management Model ↗. PLUVIA uses its own simplified engine; it does not run SWMM.

48 columns × 40 rows, meters. Land cover stays fixed.
